_comment: Example: two-arm trial with a CONTINUOUS primary endpoint (e.g. change in a biomarker or functional score), group-sequential with one interim and blinded-style conditional-power SAMPLE-SIZE RE-ESTIMATION (SSR) at the interim, no enrichment. Single hypothesis on the full population. Effect sizes are standardized (sd=1) so delta is a Cohen's d. Illustrative assumptions only.

report.title: Continuous-Endpoint Trial with Sample-Size Re-estimation
report.subtitle: Continuous endpoint | interim SSR | group-sequential
report.recommendation: Appropriate when the target effect size is uncertain; the conditional-power SSR adds patients only when the interim trend is promising but underpowered, and is capped to bound the maximum sample size.
references: Mehta CR, Pocock SJ. Adaptive increase in sample size when interim results are promising. Statistics in Medicine 2011;30(28):3267-3284.
Cui L, Hung HMJ, Wang SJ. Modification of sample size in group sequential clinical trials. Biometrics 1999;55(3):853-857.
Wassmer G, Pahlke F. rpact: Confirmatory Adaptive Clinical Trial Design and Analysis. R package.
